summary: Widow of Samuel D. Pringle of Plymouth, Pa., who raised a large family there after his death in 1847; probably John's 4th-great-grand-aunt by marriage.
bio:
Huldah Ives was born in New York about 1804. A family tree gives her parents as Josiah Ives Jr. (1770–1849), who died in Michigan, and Lucy Williams (1768–1850), who married at Plymouth on 26 March 1791, and names her brothers and sisters as Orin Almond, Martha, Lucinda, Henry B., Joseph, Josiah, Richard J. and Almon Church Ives. In 1824, at Plymouth, Luzerne Co., PA, she married Samuel D. Pringle, who died on 25 March 1847. A Joshua Lamoreaux, brother of Martha Lamoreaux, married a Martha Ives who may have been her kin, though that is only a guess.

In September 1850 the widowed "Hulda Pringle", 46, owned property worth $600 and was living in Plymouth Township two doors from James Pringle, with her children Orange, a 23-year-old teamster, Ransom, 21, Keturah, 17, Jane, 14, Lucinda, 10, and Sarah, 6. Also in the house were Lucy Ives, 87, recorded as insane and probably Huldah's mother, and a 26-year-old carpenter, Philip Minchart, almost certainly the Philip Manhart (1823–1910) who married her daughter Keturah as her second husband in 1883. Her children were Mary Ann (1826–1907), Orange, George Ransom, Elmira, born in 1831, Keturah, Hannah Jane (1836–1895), who married the engineer George Bisher on 1 January 1856, Lucinda (1841–1903) and Sarah (1843–1917).

Huldah lived in Plymouth through the censuses of 1850 to 1880. She died in Plymouth Township on 29 December 1886 and was buried in Shawnee Cemetery on 3 January 1887; her will was proved that year.

researchNotes:
Huldah Ives was born in New York about 1804. In the 1850 Plymouth Twp census (14 Sep 1850, dwelling 942/family 962, two doors from James Pringle's household): Hulda Pringle 46, F, $600, b. New York; Orange Pringle 23, teamster, PA; Ransom 21; 'Caturah' 17; Jane 14; Lucinda 10; Sarah 6; Lucy Ives 87, F (marked insane - probably her mother); Philip Minchart 26, carpenter. Her daughter Hannah J. married engineer George Bisher on 1 Jan 1856. Her will: Plymouth Boro., 1887, vol. J p.499. Joshua Lamoreaux (Martha's brother) married a Martha Ives, possibly her kin (speculative).

FamilySearch tree LH7R-KFK gives Hulda's parents as Josiah Ives Jr. (1770-1849, d. Michigan) and Lucy Williams (1768-1850), married in Plymouth on 26 Mar 1791. That fits the 'Lucy Ives, 87' in her 1850 household. The tree lists her siblings as Orin Almond, Martha, Lucinda, Henry B., Joseph, Josiah, Richard J. and Almon Church Ives. It also says she married Samuel D. Pringle (H0150) in 1824, that he died on 25 Mar 1847, and that she died in Plymouth Twp. on 29 Dec 1886 and was buried in Shawnee Cemetery on 3 Jan 1887. Her will was proved in 1887. Children in the tree: Mary Ann (b. Jan 1826, d. 1907), Orange (H0153), George Ransom (H0152), Elmira (b. 1831), Keturah (H0154), Hannah Jane (1836-1895), Lucinda (1841-1903) and Sarah (b. 1 Aug 1843, d. 1917) ([R4-S1]). The Philip Minchart, 26, a carpenter living in her house in 1850, is almost certainly the Philip Manhart (1823-1910) whom her daughter Keturah married as her second husband in 1883.
